manifest.name: Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B
manifest.blurb: A 30-block DiT over patchified video latents. Text enters by cross-attention, time by 6 AdaLN taps. The umT5 encoder and the VAE are frozen; only the DiT trains.
manifest.shape_note: Shapes for 832 × 480 × 81 frames: VAE gives [16, 21, 60, 104], the (1,2,2) patch gives 21 · 30 · 52 = 32760 tokens.

L1_pipeline.title: Sampling pipeline
L1_pipeline.subtitle: One text prompt to 81 frames. Everything in the dark bar runs once per denoising step; everything outside it runs once.

nodes.title: prompt + negative prompt
sublines: they become the two CFG branches

nodes.title: umT5-XXL encoder
nodes.note: This is the single biggest misunderstanding to avoid: the text encoder is not inside the denoising loop. It runs once and its 4096-d token states are reused at every step.

nodes.title: target_shape + seq_len
sublines: H/8 × W/8 · then /2 by the patch
nodes.note: The VAE compresses 4× in time and 8× in space; the DiT patch then halves H and W again. 81 frames → 21 latent frames.

bands.label: for t in timesteps:   WanModel(x, t, context) twice — conditional and unconditional   →   CFG mix   →   scheduler.step
bands.dim: the DiT is called 2 × N times; N is typically 40–50
bands.note: Classifier-free guidance costs a second full forward pass per step. noise_pred = uncond + scale · (cond − uncond), then the flow-matching scheduler takes one step along the velocity.

edges.label: x at t = 0 — the clean latent

notes.title: Flow matching, not DDPM
notes.text: The model predicts a velocity, not an epsilon. The scheduler (FlowUniPC or FlowDPM) integrates it from t = 1 to t = 0. That is why there is no alpha/beta schedule anywhere in the model code.

notes.title: What is frozen at training time
notes.text: umT5 and the VAE are frozen and are not even loaded during a LoRA finetune of the DiT — their outputs are cached to disk. Only WanModel's 30 blocks, the two embedders and the head carry gradients.

L1b_step.title: Inside one denoising step
L1b_step.subtitle: The body of the loop, once. This is what the dark bar on the pipeline level expands into: two forward passes, the CFG mix, and one scheduler step.

zoom_from.label: for t in timesteps: … CFG … scheduler.step

nodes.title: latents, t
sublines: the same x feeds BOTH branches
t is one scalar for this step

nodes.title: arg_null = {context_null, seq_len}
sublines: umT5 states for the NEGATIVE prompt

nodes.title: WanModel(x, t, context)
nodes.note: Both branches call the SAME weights with the same x and t — only the context differs. That is the whole of classifier-free guidance at inference.

nodes.title: WanModel(x, t, context_null)
sublines: doubles the cost of every step

nodes.title: sample_scheduler.step(noise_pred, t, latents)
sublines: moves x one notch toward t = 0
nodes.note: The scheduler, not the model, owns the trajectory. The model only ever says 'which direction'; how far to move along it is the scheduler's business.

bands.label: noise_pred  =  uncond  +  guide_scale · (cond − uncond)
bands.dim: guide_scale ≈ 5 for 1.3B — extrapolate away from the unconditional prediction
bands.note: Nothing is learned here. It is one line of arithmetic that exaggerates the difference the prompt makes. guide_scale = 1 would skip the second forward pass entirely.

notes.title: Why a step costs two forward passes
notes.text: guide_scale > 1 means the DiT runs twice per step — once with the prompt, once without. That is why N = 40 steps is 80 model calls. Wan2.2-A14B adds a third wrinkle, swapping between a high-noise and a low-noise expert at a boundary timestep; the 1.3B model has a single DiT and skips that.

notes.title: What persists across steps, and what does not
notes.text: context and context_null are computed once before the loop and never change. latents is the only state carried from step to step. Nothing is cached inside the model — every step re-attends the whole 32760-token sequence from scratch.

L2_tensors.title: How three things become tokens
L2_tensors.subtitle: One pass of WanModel.forward, before the block stack. The three streams are genuinely independent until the bottom row — where they meet with three different roles, which is the thing to take away.

nodes.title: Wan2.1 VAE · encode
sublines: at sampling, x is already latent

nodes.title: patch_embedding
nodes.note: The patch is (1,2,2): time is NOT patched. Each token is one 2×2 spatial patch of one latent frame.

nodes.title: e0 · 6 AdaLN taps
sublines: NOT a token — a modulation table

bands.label: for block in self.blocks:   x = block(x, e=e0, context=context, freqs, seq_lens, grid_sizes)
bands.dim: one call, three roles — and only x comes back out
bands.note: This is the only place the three streams touch. x is the sequence and is rewritten; context is read as K/V and returns unchanged; e0 never becomes a token at all. Repeat 30 times, then the head.

notes.title: Three streams, three roles — the asymmetry is the point
notes.text: Attention length is 32760, not 32760 + 512: text is never concatenated into the sequence, it is only ever K/V. And e0 is not a sequence at all — it is six per-channel vectors that shift, scale and gate inside each block. Only x is read and written.

notes.title: Padding to seq_len
notes.text: Each sample is right-padded with zeros to a common seq_len and the true lengths travel alongside as seq_lens, which flash-attention uses as k_lens so padding never contributes.

L3_stack.title: The block stack
L3_stack.subtitle: What enters the 30 blocks, what is shared across them, and what leaves. Shapes for 832x480x81f.

nodes.title: x · patchified latent
nodes.note: The (1,2,2) patch is the only spatial downsample inside the DiT — time is left alone, the VAE already compressed it 4×.

nodes.title: context · umT5 tokens
nodes.note: umT5-XXL itself is frozen and runs once, before the loop. Only this 2-layer projection trains.

nodes.title: e0 · 6 AdaLN taps
nodes.note: Computed once per step in float32 and handed to every block. The 6 chunks are shift/scale/gate for self-attn and for the FFN.

nodes.title: unpatchify
nodes.note: 64 = out_dim 16 × prod(patch_size) 1·2·2 — the head predicts every patch's 16 channels at once.

bands.label: WanAttentionBlock × 30   —   norm1 · self_attn (RoPE) · ⊕e₂ · norm3 · cross_attn (text K/V) · norm2 · ffn 1536→8960→1536 · ⊕e₅
bands.note: Every block gets the SAME e0, freqs and context. Only x changes. That is why the stack is one bar, not 30 boxes.

notes.title: RoPE is applied inside self_attn, per block — never here
notes.text: freqs is one buffer of 1024 rows, split across the head dim as (c − 2·⌊c/3⌋, ⌊c/3⌋, ⌊c/3⌋) for the (f, h, w) axes, then broadcast over the 3D grid. With dim 1536 / 12 heads, c = 64 complex pairs → 22/21/21.

notes.title: Text never gets RoPE and never gets modulated
notes.text: cross_attn takes norm3(x) as Q and the raw context as K/V. The 6 AdaLN taps only touch the video stream — see e[0..2] on self-attn and e[3..5] on the FFN inside the block.

zoom_from.label: the three inputs enter the stack

L4_block.title: Inside one block — the exact order
L4_block.subtitle: WanAttentionBlock.forward, top to bottom, in execution order. Read the left column as the residual stream; the right columns are what feeds in.

nodes.title: modulation + e → chunk(6)
sublines: added to the shared e0, split into 6
nodes.note: Each block owns its own `modulation` parameter. e0 is shared across all 30 blocks; this per-block bias is what makes block i modulate differently from block j. Computed in float32.

nodes.title: norm1 = WanLayerNorm
nodes.note: Deliberately affine-free: the gain and bias come from the timestep instead, in the next step. That is what makes it adaptive LayerNorm.

nodes.title: self_attn — WanSelfAttention
sublines: q, k, v · QK-RMSNorm · 3D RoPE · flash
nodes.note: RoPE is applied here, inside the attention, to q and k only — never to the residual stream and never to the text.

nodes.title: x = x + y · e[2]
sublines: initialised so the block starts near-identity

nodes.title: norm3 = WanLayerNorm
nodes.note: The one norm in the block that HAS its own affine parameters — it is not modulated by the timestep.

nodes.title: cross_attn — WanCrossAttention
sublines: Q from x, K/V from context

nodes.title: x = x + cross_attn(…)
sublines: NO gate here — the only ungated residual
nodes.note: Asymmetry worth noticing: self-attention and the MLP are gated by e[2] and e[5], but cross-attention is added straight. Text conditioning is never gated off by the timestep.

nodes.title: × (1 + e[4]) + e[3]
sublines: the MLP's own shift and scale

nodes.title: ffn — the MLP
nodes.note: A plain 2-layer MLP with GELU — NOT SwiGLU, and no gate projection. Wan differs from Llama-style blocks here.

notes.title: The order in one line
notes.text: norm1 → modulate → SELF-ATTN → gated add → norm3 → CROSS-ATTN → plain add → norm2 → modulate → MLP → gated add.  Pre-norm throughout: every sublayer normalises its input, never its output, and the residual stream is never normalised.

notes.title: Where the 6 taps go
notes.text: e[0] shift and e[1] scale feed self-attention's input; e[2] gates its output. e[3] shift and e[4] scale feed the MLP's input; e[5] gates its output. Cross-attention gets none of them.

notes.title: Three precision boundaries
notes.text: The modulation arithmetic and both gated residuals run under an explicit float32 autocast, and the norms cast to float32 internally before casting back. Everything else runs in bf16. Getting this wrong is a classic source of drift in a finetune.

L5_attention.title: Attention level — self vs cross, side by side
L5_attention.subtitle: Both are WanSelfAttention; WanCrossAttention subclasses it and overrides only forward. Same weights shape, three real differences.

nodes.title: q, k, v  ← all from x
q ← x,   k, v ← context
sublines: but K and V read the TEXT
nodes.note: This single substitution is the whole of cross-attention. Everything else is inherited unchanged from WanSelfAttention.

nodes.title: norm_q / norm_k = WanRMSNorm
nodes.note: Note the ordering: the RMSNorm runs on the flat 1536-d projection, then .view() splits it into 12 heads. It is not a per-head norm.

nodes.title: none
nodes.note: Cross-attention is permutation-invariant over the text tokens as far as this module is concerned — any ordering information is already baked into the umT5 states.

nodes.title: flash_attention(q, k, v)
nodes.note: This is the quadratic term and essentially the whole cost of the model: 32760² per head × 12 heads × 30 blocks, twice per step for CFG.

nodes.title: flash_attention(q, k, v)
nodes.note: 64× cheaper than self-attention here, because K/V length is 512 instead of 32760.

notes.title: The three differences, and nothing else
notes.text: 1 — K and V read context instead of x.  2 — no RoPE on either side.  3 — k_lens is the text length, not the video length. The projections, the QK-RMSNorm, the kernel and the output projection are literally the same code path.

notes.title: No GQA, no KV cache
notes.text: q, k and v are all full width (1536 → 1536, 12 heads each) — this is plain MHA, not grouped-query. A diffusion model re-attends the whole sequence every step, so there is nothing to cache.

L6_subops.title: Sub-operations
L6_subops.subtitle: The three pieces worth reading on their own: how 3D RoPE is built and applied, which attention kernel actually runs, and how tokens become pixels again.

nodes.title: rope_params(max_seq_len, dim, θ=10000)
nodes.note: Built once in __init__ as a buffer, for three axes concatenated: dim − 2·⌊dim/3⌋ for frames, ⌊dim/3⌋ each for height and width. With head_dim 128 that is 22 / 21 / 21 complex pairs.

nodes.title: rope_apply(x, grid_sizes, freqs)
sublines: split freqs into (f, h, w) bands
nodes.note: Runs in float64 under a disabled-autocast decorator. Each token's rotation is the concatenation of its frame, row and column rotations — that is what makes it 3D rather than 1D RoPE.

nodes.title: flash_attention(...)
sublines: varlen: packs the batch into one sequence
nodes.note: q_lens / k_lens let padded samples share a kernel launch without padding ever attending. half() casts to bf16 — the kernel does not take fp32.

nodes.title: attention(...) — the fallback
nodes.note: Worth knowing when you compare runs across machines: without FlashAttention installed, the padding mask is silently disabled and the numbers can differ.

expect.first: 'Padding mask is disabled when using scaled_dot_product_attention. It can have a significant impact on performance.'

nodes.title: Head
nodes.note: A second, smaller AdaLN — 2 taps instead of 6, since there is no gate and no second sublayer. It consumes e, not e0.

notes.title: Why the patch is (1, 2, 2) and the head outputs 64
notes.text: Each token covers one latent frame and a 2×2 spatial patch. The head must therefore predict 16 channels × 4 positions = 64 numbers per token, and unpatchify scatters them back onto the grid. Change the patch size and both numbers move together.

notes.title: RMSNorm vs LayerNorm in this model
notes.text: WanRMSNorm (learnable gain, no mean subtraction) is used only for QK-norm inside attention. WanLayerNorm (usually affine-free) is used for every block norm and for the head. They are not interchangeable here.
